label: internal tools
title: Apple
description: Apple — case study by Christian Jeria.
summary: Apple's Industrial Design group, led by Jony Ive, defines the physical form of every Apple product — from iPhone to MacBook to Apple Watch.
overview: For four years, I worked as a Human Interface Designer at Apple embedded within the Industrial Design group — Jony Ive's team. My focus was not on consumer-facing software, but on the internal tools and workflows that helped one of the world's most demanding design teams do their best work.

Working at this level meant operating at the intersection of design craft and engineering, understanding deeply how industrial designers think, and translating that into software that felt invisible — tools that got out of the way and let the work speak for itself.

label: hardware · fleet app
title: Origin Labs
description: Origin Labs — case study by Christian Jeria.
summary: A 3D printing startup that built the Origin One, a manufacturing-grade printer using Programmable PhotoPolymerization (P³) technology — later acquired by Stratasys.
overview: Origin was a 3D printing startup that developed the Origin One, a manufacturing-grade 3D printer utilizing Programmable PhotoPolymerization (P³) technology. I was hired to design the company logo and the user interfaces for both the embedded system on the printer and the web application used to manage a fleet of printers.

label: mobile · web3
title: MetaMask
description: MetaMask — case study by Christian Jeria.
summary: A secure, user-friendly wallet and gateway to the decentralized web, trusted by tens of millions of monthly active users worldwide.
overview: Over the course of several years at MetaMask, I helped shape the experience of one of the world's most widely used web3 products. My work spanned onboarding, wallet interactions, and decentralized app transactions, designing for both seasoned crypto users and those brand new to the space. I also created the now-iconic MetaMask fox logo and mascot, which has become a recognizable symbol of web3 itself.

Featured here is a selection of projects where I led product design and creative direction, with the goal of making decentralized technologies more intuitive, trustworthy, and accessible to millions of people worldwide.

label: wallet · brand
title: Portal
description: Portal — case study by Christian Jeria.
summary: An early-stage startup building and testing wallet service concepts for web3.
overview: At PortalHQ, I partnered with the team to bring early product concepts to life through rapid prototyping and design exploration. My contributions spanned across product, marketing, and brand presence: helping the company validate ideas for wallet services, shaping product illustrations, supporting marketing campaigns, and fully maintaining and evolving their website.

label: web · knowledge graph
title: Intuition Systems
description: Intuition Systems — case study by Christian Jeria.
summary: A knowledge network where people make claims about anything — ideas, facts, opinions — and the community supports or challenges them by investing in them using crypto.
overview: At the start of 2025, I joined Intuition as Lead Product Designer to help the team unify a series of failed experiments into one flagship product. Their first attempt, Portal, had been confusing, overloaded, and lacked a clear value proposition. With no strategy or roadmap in place, my role was to bring clarity, focus, and design leadership to shape a cohesive experience. The goal was simple: turn scattered ideas into a product users could actually understand and love.

label: motion · AI assistant
title: Mobina
description: Mobina — motion design project by Christian Jeria.
summary: A motion design piece introducing Mobina, an AI executive assistant that handles scheduling, inboxes, and busywork so people can focus on what matters.

overview: Mobina is an AI executive assistant that manages the day-to-day busywork of running a calendar and inbox — scheduling, follow-ups, and coordination — so people can spend their time on higher-leverage work.
I directed and animated a product video for Mobina, translating what the assistant does into a short piece of motion design: clear, confident, and built to explain the product at a glance.
